title: introduce-slot-throttle-fabric-and-minimum-throughput-guarantee-adapter
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds slot-based soft-throttling fabric with minimum throughput guarantees and new utilization-delta exporter. Behavior is opt-in via fleet configuration. No breaking changes by default.
description:
Context and motivation: Large customers on Dedicated reported transient SLA violations when microbursts from noisy tenants caused long tail latency and short-term throughput starvation for other tenants. Existing reservation and warm-pool mechanisms reduced tail events but lacked a graceful, low-latency enforcement layer that could (a) shape headroom at sub-second granularity, (b) preserve minimum throughput guarantees for committed tenants, and (c) surface utilization drift telemetry for capacity tuning. This PR implements a slot-throttle fabric plus a minimum-throughput guarantee adapter and a utilization-delta exporter to address these gaps.

Design summary: 1) Slot throttle fabric: a lightweight in-process controller that subdivides pool capacity into fixed-size "slots" and enforces per-tenant slot consumption rates. Slots are a logical unit (not pinned GPUs) that allow soft throttling with configurable window sizes and decay. The fabric exposes token-bucket semantics for short-term bursts while integrating with the existing warm-pool and reservation layers. 2) Minimum throughput guarantee adapter: an admission/time-slicing adapter that ensures tenants with committed throughput receive a best-effort minimum over a rolling SLA window, moving excess slots away from opportunistic tenants when necessary. Guarantees are expressed as a fractional throughput quota per pool and can be overridden per-tenant via fleet config. 3) Utilization-delta exporter: new telemetry that computes per-tenant utilization delta across configurable windows (100ms, 1s, 10s) and emits Prometheus metrics + an optional structured trace event. This helps ops tune slot sizing and decay policies.

API & config changes: - config/fleet/throughput_policy.yaml: new fields: slot_size, slot_window_ms, slot_decay_ms, min_throughput_fraction, guarantee_window_seconds, enforcement_mode (off/soft/hard) - scheduler/admission: new hook registerSlotThrottle() used by Dedicated autoscaler when pool_type == "slot-fabric" - observability: metrics new: redwood_slot_allocations_total, redwood_slot_reclaims_total, redwood_util_delta_seconds, redwood_min_throughput_violations_total

Files changed (high level): src/autoscaler/slot_throttle_fabric.go, pkg/scheduler/min_throughput_adapter.go, telemetry/util_delta_exporter.go, config/defaults/throughput_policy.yaml, cmd/operator/templates/throughput_policy_crd.yaml, tests/unit/slot_throttle_test.go, tests/integration/min_throughput_integration_test.go, docs/operator/throughput_guarantees.md, e2e/dedicated/slot_fabric_smoke.yaml

Compatibility & rollout: The new fabric is opt-in. No config is changed by default. Operators can enable per-pool by setting pool.metadata.policy = slot-fabric and tuning slot_window_ms. Rollout plan: 1) canary enable on a small warm-pool (non-critical customers) 2) monitor redwood_util_delta_seconds and redwood_min_throughput_violations_total for 48h 3) gradually expand, adjusting slot_size and decay. For fleets with strict guarantees, enforcement_mode: soft is recommended initially.

Testing: - Unit: slot allocation/reclaim, decay logic, adapter correctness (edge cases around fractional guarantees) - Integration: multi-tenant integration test where an opportunistic tenant surges and committed tenants maintain min throughput under enforced mode - E2E: smoke config in k8s with 2 small pools (canary) - Load test: synthetic burst harness validated a 62% reduction in 95th p99 latency amplification for non-committed tenants while committed tenants maintained >=99% of their min_throughput_fraction over 10s windows.

Observability / debugging: Added structured logging when slots are reclaimed or when a guarantee is degraded (log id includes pool, tenant_id, window_start, window_end, expected_vs_actual). Utilization-delta exporter includes labels: pool, tenant, region, enforcement_mode. Dashboards: docs include an example Grafana panel and an alert rule suggestion (Alert when redwood_min_throughput_violations_total > 5 in 5m).

Backward compat & migration notes: No migration required. Fleet managers must opt-in to slot-fabric. When disabling, system reverts to previous reservation/warm-pool behavior with no data loss.

Security: No new secrets. The exporter uses existing metrics plumbing; no elevated permissions required.

Related work: builds on top of prior warm-pool hedging and reservation controllers (ENG-1829 / pr-314653). This PR focuses on fine-grained short-window shaping and telemetry rather than long-window reservations.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached (docs/operator/throughput_guarantees.md) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Load test results (bench/load/slot_fabric/) - [x] Operator CRD template updated - [x] Release notes entry prepared

b7d2a90: min_throughput_adapter with rolling-window enforcement and tests
c9e5f11: add util-delta exporter, docs, and operator CRD templates; address linting feedback
review_thread: Janelle Kim (review): Can we avoid allocating slot structs on the hot path? Suggest switch to a small ring buffer and index math. Response: refactored allocation to use preallocated ring, reduced GC pressure in benchmark.
Ravi Srinivasan (review): What about tenant burst reclassification to opportunistic after sustained overshoot? Response: added reclassification thresholds; documented behavior in operator docs.
Marco Li (review): lint: prefer context-aware logging. Response: addressed and tweaked log fields; added unit for log formatting. Approved after fixes.
notes_for_ops: Enable per-pool with: pool.metadata.policy=slot-fabric; tune slot_window_ms and slot_size. Start in enforcement_mode=soft. Watch redwood_util_delta_seconds and redwood_min_throughput_violations_total. For high-noise tenants, increase slot_decay_ms to lengthen smoothing.
